THE POINT ST. CHARLES INSTITUTE'S BENEFACTORS PAGE, 1895
=========================================================
Recovered 2026-09-06 under p_430 by the INDEX-FORM query "Charlton, R. L." (24 hits; the running form
"R. L. Charlton" is lost in a much larger set). Open Library search-inside; the item is a CIHM
microform, `cihm_04413`, *Report of the Point St. Charles Institute* (Montreal, 1895). NOT READ —
the page below is four overlapping phrase queries stitched together.

THE PAGE, as the queries returned it
------------------------------------
  "...enrolled in each annual report."
  LIFE BENEFACTORS
      CHARLES CUSHING
      ROBERTSON MACAULAY
      T. B. MACAULAY
      JAMES COCHRANE
  BENEFACTORS. 1894-95.
      Alexander, Chas.      Charlton, R. L.
      Ames, H. B.           Cowan, Robt.
      Armstrong, Dr.        Dougall, John & Son
  (the OCR prints the year as "1804-95" and Ames as "HH. B.")

WHY IT MATTERS
--------------
Five of this project's people on one page, in the camp's founding year:

  R. L. CHARLTON      Kanawana's first camp committee, 1894 ("Summer Camp. John W. Ross, Chairman.
                      E. J. Coyle. R. L. Charlton"), and the man a 1951 source credits with proposing
                      the name Kanawana.
  H. B. AMES          the reformer already in founding-1894.md as a fellow member of the Ontario and
                      Quebec Provincial Committee of February 1891, with Charlton and D. A. Budge.
  CHARLES CUSHING     notary son of Lemuel Cushing, who took boys to Lake Saint-Joseph in 1892; he
                      married Lily Macaulay, Robertson Macaulay's daughter — and here he is listed
                      immediately before his father-in-law and brother-in-law.
  ROBERTSON MACAULAY  Sun Life president; with T. B. Macaulay, his son and successor.
  CHAS. ALEXANDER     the name of the confectioner who founded the Boys' Home of Montreal in 1870 —
                      later Weredale House, whose camp became Camp Lewis and then Camp Weredale.

Kanawana's founders, the Boys' Home's founder and the Macaulays, subscribing to the same settlement
mission in the same year. This project had those three strands separately and no document holding
them together.

WHAT IS NOT PROVED
------------------
Three of the five are NAME MATCHES joined by city, date and milieu — "Alexander, Chas.", "Charlton,
R. L." and "Charles Cushing" are common forms. The Macaulay pair is near-certain, appearing in that
order throughout the Sun Life literature. And nothing here mentions a camp, so p_456's question —
whether the YMCA's Camp Macaulay of 1932 was a donor naming — is made more plausible and is not
answered.

METHOD NOTE. The index form is what found this, again: "Charlton, R. L." returns 24 items where the
running form drowns. Same inversion that produced Owens's day job (f_5204) and Patton's Naismith
biography (f_5205).
